holidays.name: National Bobblehead Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the wobbly-headed collectibles that nod along from desks, dashboards, and ballpark shelves. Give your favorite bobblehead a tiny salute, or start a collection.
holidays.origin: It is an unofficial pop-culture observance. Bobbleheads have been around for generations and became hugely popular as sports giveaways.
holidays.funFact: Bobbleheads are sometimes called nodders. Their springs or weighted necks make the head keep bouncing long after you tap it.

holidays.name: National Pass Gas Day
holidays.description: A cheeky, lighthearted observance that treats a perfectly natural bodily function with humor. It lands the day after National Bean Day, which is no coincidence.
holidays.origin: It is an unofficial observance with no documented founder. It caught on as a joking follow-up to National Bean Day on January 6.
holidays.funFact: Beans are famous for causing gas because they contain complex sugars that people can't fully digest. Gut bacteria ferment those sugars instead.

holidays.name: National Tempura Day
holidays.description: A crispy celebration of Japan's light, airy batter-fried shrimp and vegetables. It's a good excuse to dunk something in dipping sauce.
holidays.origin: It is an unofficial food observance celebrating the Japanese frying technique. Its founder is unclear.
holidays.funFact: Tempura is widely thought to have been introduced to Japan by Portuguese traders in the 16th century. It became a signature Japanese dish over time.
